note: The scripted conversation for Sublab Medium, and the probes asked after it. The turn whose text is exactly "<compress>" is the command, not something the applicant said: when you run the comparison, that turn is where your compress() runs. In the run without compression, skip that turn entirely so both runs send the same twelve turns.
conversation: Сәлеметсіз бе! My name is Daniyar Qoshan, applicant A-202.
I sent my transcript last week. Do I qualify for the study grant?
My income band is 2 - my family's certificate says so.
So how much would that come to, if it goes through?
I could not upload my id card because the scanner at home broke.
I can only come to the office on Thursdays, I have lab all week otherwise.
Also, does a scanned letter from my employer count, or does it have to be the original?
Understood. And if I bring the id card on Thursday, will the decision be made the same day?
One more thing - my sister Aruzhan applied last year and she is on file too.
Sorry, where were we? What is still missing from my file?
And what was the amount again?

probes.question: Which applicant am I, and what is my number?
Which document is still missing from my file?
What is my income band, and what amount does that come to?
probes.tests: the band from turn 3 and the amount from turn 4

probes.question: Which day of the week can I come to the office?
probes.tests: a constraint the applicant stated in turn 6 and never repeated

probes.question: What did I ask you about my employer?
probes.tests: an open question, turn 7, never answered

why_these_probes: Each probe asks for something said exactly once and never repeated, so a summary has to decide to keep it. Q-4 and Q-5 are the interesting ones: a fluent summary drops a constraint and an unanswered question first, because neither is about the decision. For each probe, expect_contains is what the answer must contain to count as retrieved - short checkable strings, not a judgement call. Report per probe: retrieved or lost, and the reply you got.
